lines.summary: fix(fonts): evict atlas pages between frames; Korean fallback with block-gated lazy loads (#100)
lines.text: Text, Button and TextInput take any `fontSize` in pixels, and text is UTF-8. Without `font` they use the runtime's DejaVu Sans. Characters a `.ttf` or `.otf` font lacks render in DejaVu Sans, then in Droid Sans Fallback Full (Chinese and Japanese) or Noto Sans KR (Korean); a character none of them has renders as a box. `.fnt` and `.bdf` fonts have no fallback.

lines.summary: feat(fonts): colour emoji from Twemoji in the glyph atlas (#91)
lines.text: Emoji render in colour, sized to `fontSize`, from the [Twemoji](https://github.com/jdecked/twemoji) images (CC-BY 4.0) that ship with VitaDeck. Single emoji, emoji with `U+FE0F`, skin tones, flags and keycaps work. A ZWJ sequence Twemoji has no image for draws as its first emoji, and a symbol such as `❤` without `U+FE0F` stays a font glyph. `.fnt` and `.bdf` fonts draw no emoji.

lines.text: `getItem(key)` returns `null` for a missing key. `setItem` and `removeItem` return once the change is on disk. Each Deck App gets 1 MiB; a `setItem` that would go past it throws a `RangeError` and keeps the previous value. Reinstalling the Deck App over Runtime Upload keeps its storage; removing it in the VitaDeck Shell deletes it.

lines.text: - On the desktop build, arrow keys and Enter are the D-pad and Cross; Backspace, T, S, L and R are Circle, Triangle, Square, L and R; hovering a `Button` with the mouse focuses it. The full table is under [Host mappings](https://github.com/matemolnar8/vitadeck/blob/main/CONTEXT.md#host-mappings).

lines.summary: feat(input): TextInput with Vita IME dialog and host keyboard editing (#86)
lines.text: `TextInput` is a controlled single-line field. Pressing it starts an edit: the Vita opens its keyboard dialog, pre-filled with `value` and titled with `placeholder`; the desktop build edits in place, where you type, Backspace deletes, Enter confirms and Escape cancels. `onChange` fires once with the final text when the edit is confirmed; a cancelled edit fires nothing.
